items.stem: What does your BATNA represent in a negotiation?

options.text: Your best alternative if no agreement is reached
options.rationale: Correct: BATNA is your best option away from the table and sets your walkaway power.

options.text: The maximum you are willing to pay
options.rationale: That is closer to your reservation price, not your BATNA.
BATNA is your own alternative, not their offer.
BATNA is independent of the other party's position.

items.explanation: Correct: BATNA is your best option away from the table and sets your walkaway power.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO moves help create value (integrative bargaining) rather than just claim it? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Trade issues each side values differently
options.rationale: Correct: logrolling across differing priorities expands the pie.

options.text: Ask questions to uncover the other side's interests
options.rationale: Correct: understanding interests reveals mutual-gain options.

options.text: Make the first demand as extreme as possible
options.rationale: Extreme anchoring is a value-claiming, not value-creating, move.
Withholding all information blocks mutual-gain trades.

items.explanation: Correct: trading across differences and surfacing interests create value.

items.stem: A counterpart opens with an extreme anchor. What is a sound response?

options.text: Decline to counter near the anchor and re-anchor with your own justified number
options.rationale: Correct: resetting with a reasoned counter avoids being pulled toward their anchor.

options.text: Immediately split the difference with their anchor
options.rationale: Splitting from an extreme anchor concedes too much.
Accepting an extreme anchor sacrifices your interests.
An aggressive anchor is a tactic to manage, not an automatic dealbreaker.

items.explanation: Correct: resetting with a reasoned counter avoids being pulled toward their anchor.
